```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
```

```{r}
#| label: entries
#| include: false

# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file.
#
# Section 1 of this note mirrors the errata page of the book website,
# https://book.declaredesign.org/errata.html, entry for entry and in the page's order, under
# the page's three subheadings (`part`): 16 under "Errata", 1 under "Substantive changes",
# and 4 under "Code updates". The page is the authors' record and this note does not add to
# it or reorder it, so the numbering follows the page and not the severity blocks that
# PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b prescribes elsewhere. Every entry is source "publisher_record": the
# finding was published by the authors on the book's own website, and none was found by this
# programme's pipeline or reading.
#
# No entry names a claim id. The book's outputs are figures and Monte Carlo diagnosands, so
# the repository holds no extraction of printed numbers, and no entry is class quantity.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, which each renderer turns into its own markup (bold
# here). Inside a code span the span is left unmarked, because a marker there would print as
# literal asterisks.
#
# A note may carry a classification rationale after "Class note: ". The rationale is kept in
# the CSV and is not printed, so that Section 1 reads as the website's page does.
#
# Section 2 is the reference-list errata (part "Reference list", source "reference_audit"),
# found by the Crossref audit of the bibliography and not on the website.
#
# Section 3, the changes made to the code that draws the figures, is NOT errata and is not in
# this table. It is read from code_updates/ at render time.

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~part, ~class, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note,

  1, "Errata", "cross_reference", "full",
```

# Issues with the printed book

`r str_to_sentence(number_word)` entries, in the order of the errata page of the book website, [book.declaredesign.org/errata.html](https://book.declaredesign.org/errata.html), under its three headings. The authors published every entry; this note carries them unchanged. Bold marks the tokens that changed in prose; a change inside code is stated in words. The book is *Research Design in the Social Sciences: Declaration, Diagnosis, and Redesign* (Princeton University Press, 2023; ISBN 9780691199573, no DOI), by Graeme Blair, Alexander Coppock, and Macartan Humphreys. The repository `active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_humphreys_2023` verifies and maintains the book's deposited code at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_humphreys_2023](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/blair_coppock_humphreys_2023), archived at Zenodo as [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24168284](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168284).

```{r}
#| label: render-entries
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every one opens with one.
subheading <- c("Errata" = "Errata", "Substantive changes" = "Substantive changes",
                "Code updates" = "Code updates")
lead_in <- c(
  "Errata" = "These errata are errors in the printed book. These changes are implemented in the online version.",
  "Substantive changes" = NA_character_,
  "Code updates" = str_c(
    "We are committed to maintaining the code in this book as the R ecosystem evolves. ",
    "The following changes reflect differences between the printed book and the online version."
  )
)

render_entry <- function(e) {
  cat("\n\n### ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, " (", e$location, ")\n\n> ", bold(e$published), sep = "")
  if (!is.na(e$corrected)) cat("\n\n**Corrected:** ", bold(e$corrected), sep = "")
  shown <- if (is.na(e$note)) NA_character_ else str_split_i(e$note, fixed("\n\nClass note: "), 1)
  if (!is.na(shown) && !str_starts(e$note, "Class note: ")) cat("\n\n", shown, sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}

walk(names(subheading), function(p) {
  cat("\n\n## ", subheading[[p]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.na(lead_in[[p]])) cat(lead_in[[p]], "\n", sep = "")
  walk(seq_len(nrow(entries)), function(i) {
    if (entries$part[i] == p) render_entry(entries[i, ])
  })
})
```

*Due to final copyediting by the Press, the website version may differ slightly from the print version. If you discover a discrepancy, please email the authors at graeme.blair@gmail.com, acoppock@gmail.com, and macartan@gmail.com.*

# Errors in the reference list

These errata are not on the book website. They come from an audit of the book's bibliography against the Crossref record of each cited work, and each is a page range or an author list that the record contradicts.

```{r}
#| label: render-references
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

walk(seq_len(nrow(entries)), function(i) {
  if (entries$part[i] == "Reference list") render_entry(entries[i, ])
})
```

# Changes to the code that draws the figures

These are not errata. They describe the figure scripts in the deposited replication archive, [doi.org/10.7910/DVN/HYVPO5](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/HYVPO5), and not code printed in the book. They are not on the book website and they are not counted in `errata_entries.csv` or in any errata total. The repository generates them from its reproduction ground truth, in `code_updates/build_code_updates.R`.

```{r}
#| label: code-updates
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

code_updates <- read_lines(here::here("code_updates", "blair_coppock_humphreys_2023_code_updates.md"))
first <- which(str_detect(code_updates, "^[0-9]+ of the [0-9]+ figure scripts"))
stopifnot(length(first) == 1)
body <- code_updates[first:length(code_updates)]
body <- body[body != "## Bullets"]
# Bullets are written one per line with no blank line between them, so each needs its own.
cat("\n", str_c(body[nzchar(body)], collapse = "\n\n"), "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: emit-spine
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof")),
  !any(entries$class == "quantity")
)

# Every [[...]] span is closed, and none sits inside a code span.
stopifnot(
  !any(str_detect(c(entries$published, entries$corrected), "`[^`]*\\[\\[[^`]*`"), na.rm = TRUE)
)

# The four code updates are printed in Section 1, because the website prints them, but they
# are not errata and are left out of the spine: each replaces printed code with a package's
# current interface and states no wrong claim. Entry numbers are kept, so the spine skips
# 18 to 21.
entries |>
  filter(part != "Code updates") |>
  select(entry, class, source, form, title, location, published, corrected, note,
         claim_ids, corrected_values, values_in_spans) |>
  write_csv(here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
